This posting passes all five criteria when the rules are applied strictly, though level is a borderline call.

(1) Role type: The title is Research Engineer / Scientist, and the content describes the role as a 'Research Engineer on Alignment Science'. The representative projects are mostly hands-on engineering: training language models to subvert safety techniques, running multi-agent RL experiments, building tooling to evaluate LLM-generated jailbreaks, and writing scripts and prompts to generate evaluation questions. Contributing to papers is only one of several listed activities. This fits the Research Engineer exception: the work is mainly building and training systems, not publishing novel research. 'Research Engineer' is also in target_roles. Her co-op work on evaluated retrieval-augmented QA, fine-tuning a transformer classifier with MLflow experiment tracking, and her rag-eval-lab project map directly onto building evaluation tooling and running ML experiments.

(2) Level: There is no explicit requirement for 3+ years of experience, no mid or senior label, and no PhD requirement. The minimum education is a Bachelor's degree or equivalent, and years of experience are tied to an unstated internal level. She is finishing an MS in CS (AI concentration) at Boston University in 2026-12 and has an 8-month ML Engineer co-op, so she meets the stated minimums. One caveat: the phrase 'significant software, ML, or research engineering experience' and the $350K–$500K salary range suggest the bar may be above a typical new grad. These are not explicit disqualifiers under the rules, and the posting says candidates 'need not have 100% of the skills'.

(3) Skills: The required 'You may be a good fit if you' section names no specific technologies. Python appears only as the interview language, and Kubernetes and LLMs appear only under the optional 'Strong candidates may also' section. Because fewer than 2 technologies are required, the skills test is skipped. Python, which she has shipped, matches the interview language anyway. Kubernetes is in her familiar_with_not_shipped list, but here it is only a nice-to-have, not a core requirement.

(4) Location: The role is in San Francisco, CA, which is US-based, with a hybrid policy of at least 25% in office and a preference for the Bay Area. She is based in Boston and is willing to relocate within the US.

(5) Sponsorship: The posting states 'We do sponsor visas!' and promises every reasonable effort to obtain one. She needs sponsorship, and the posting does not disclaim it.

Conclusion: RELEVANT. The strongest risk is the seniority implied by 'significant experience' and the compensation band.
